proposals.before: When Liu Wuzhou rebelled, Jingde served him as a deputy general; marching south with Song Jingang, they seized Jin and Fen prefectures.
proposals.after: When Liu Wuzhou rebelled, Jingde served him as a deputy general; marching south with Song Jingang, they seized Jin and Hui prefectures.
proposals.reason: Chinese 澮 is Hui, not Fen (汾); both English fields render the wrong prefecture.

proposals.before: When Liu Wuzhou rose, Jingde was made a deputy general; with Song Jingang he invaded south and captured the two prefectures of Jin and Fen.
proposals.after: When Liu Wuzhou rose, Jingde was made a deputy general; with Song Jingang he invaded south and captured the two prefectures of Jin and Hui.
proposals.reason: Chinese 晉、澮二州 names Hui (澮), not Fen.

proposals.before: In Wude year 3, when the Prince of Qin attacked Wuzhou at Baiyu, Wuzhou sent Jingde and Song Jingang to block the imperial army at Jiexiu.
proposals.after: In Wude year 3, when the Prince of Qin attacked Wuzhou at Baibi, Wuzhou sent Jingde and Song Jingang to block the imperial army at Jiexiu.
proposals.reason: 柏壁 is Baibi, not Baiyu.

proposals.before: In the third year of Wude, Taizong attacked Wuzhou at Baiyu; Wuzhou ordered Jingde and Song Jingang to meet the imperial army at Jiexiu.
proposals.after: In the third year of Wude, Taizong attacked Wuzhou at Baibi; Wuzhou ordered Jingde and Song Jingang to meet the imperial army at Jiexiu.
proposals.reason: 柏壁 is Baibi, not Baiyu.

proposals.before: Qu Tuotong, left vice director of the executive department, and Yin Kaishan, a minister, both urged: "Jingde has only just come over; his loyalty is still uncertain.
proposals.after: Qutu Tong, left vice director of the executive department, and Yin Kaishan, a minister, both urged: "Jingde has only just come over; his loyalty is still uncertain.
proposals.reason: 屈突 is the compound surname Qutu; Qu Tuotong splits the name incorrectly.

proposals.before: When Dou Jiande camped at Banzhu, the prince prepared an ambush with Li Jiji, Cheng Zhijie, Qin Shubao, and others before offering battle.
proposals.after: When Dou Jiande camped at Banzhu, the prince prepared an ambush with Li Ji, Cheng Zhijie, Qin Shubao, and others before offering battle.
proposals.reason: 李勣 is Li Ji, not Li Jiji.

proposals.before: When Dou Jiande encamped at Banzhu, Taizong was about to offer battle and first hid the troops of Li Jiji, Cheng Zhijie, Qin Shubao, and others.
proposals.after: When Dou Jiande encamped at Banzhu, Taizong was about to offer battle and first hid the troops of Li Ji, Cheng Zhijie, Qin Shubao, and others.
proposals.reason: 李勣 is Li Ji, not Li Jiji.

proposals.before: Then Li Jiji and the hidden force charged and smashed Dou's army.
proposals.after: Then Li Ji and the hidden force charged and smashed Dou's army.
proposals.reason: 勣 is the given name Ji; Li Jiji is a mistransliteration.

proposals.before: Jingde volunteered to take it; with Gao Zaosheng and Liang Jianfang he charged straight into the enemy ranks, seized Wang Wan and his horse, and rode back unopposed.
proposals.after: Jingde volunteered to take it; with Gao Zengsheng and Liang Jianfang he charged straight into the enemy ranks, seized Wang Wan and his horse, and rode back unopposed.
proposals.reason: 高甑生 is Gao Zengsheng; Zaosheng misreads 甑.

proposals.before: Jingde asked to go and seize it; then with Gao Zaosheng and Liang Jianfang the three riders plunged straight into the rebel army, captured Wan, led his horse back, and none of the rebel host dared oppose them.
proposals.after: Jingde asked to go and seize it; then with Gao Zengsheng and Liang Jianfang the three riders plunged straight into the rebel army, captured Wan, led his horse back, and none of the rebel host dared oppose them.
proposals.reason: 高甑生 is Gao Zengsheng, not Gao Zaosheng.

proposals.before: Left Vice Director of the Executive Department Qu Tuotong and Minister Yin Kaishan both said: "Jingde has only lately submitted to the state; his feelings are not yet attached.
proposals.after: Left Vice Director of the Executive Department Qutu Tong and Minister Yin Kaishan both said: "Jingde has only lately submitted to the state; his feelings are not yet attached.
proposals.reason: 屈突 is the compound surname Qutu; Qu Tuotong splits the name incorrectly.

proposals.before: Thereupon with Jiji and the others they struck fiercely and routed them utterly.
proposals.after: Thereupon with Ji and the others they struck fiercely and routed them utterly.
proposals.reason: Chinese 勣 is the given name Ji, not Jiji.

proposals.before: Crown Prince Li Jiancheng and Prince of Qi Li Yuanji plotted against the Prince of Qin and secretly wrote to win Jingde over: "We hope you will turn from my brother's service and befriend us as equals—may we have what we ask."
proposals.after: The Hidden Crown Prince and the Nest-stinging Prince Yuanji plotted to harm Taizong and secretly wrote to win Jingde over: "We wish to divert the elder's regard and cultivate a commoner's friendship; may we have what we hope."
proposals.reason: Chinese names them 隱太子 and 巢剌王元吉, not Qi; the letter asks to divert an elder's regard, not to leave a brother's service.

proposals.before: Jingde refused: "I come from humble obscurity; when the Sui fell and the realm collapsed I had nowhere to turn and long served rebels—a crime that deserved death.
proposals.after: Jingde refused: "I come from humble obscurity; when the Sui fell and the realm collapsed I had nowhere to turn and long served rebels—a crime for which even execution could not atone.
proposals.reason: 罪不容誅 means the crime is too great for execution to suffice, not merely that death was deserved.

proposals.before: Yuanji denounced him to Emperor Gaozu, who had Jingde jailed for trial and execution; only the prince's desperate plea saved him.
proposals.after: Yuanji denounced him to Emperor Gaozu, who had Jingde jailed for interrogation and was going to kill him; Taizong's firm remonstrance secured his release.
proposals.reason: 固諫 is firm remonstrance by 太宗, not an unnamed prince's desperate plea.

proposals.before: Taizong's mount again bolted into the woods below; it was caught crosswise by what tethered it and fell, unable to rise.
proposals.after: Taizong's mount again bolted into the woods below; it was caught crosswise by what tethered it, and he fell, unable to rise.
proposals.reason: 墜不能興 refers to Taizong being thrown and unable to get up, not the horse remaining down.

proposals.before: Jiancheng's generals Xue Wanche, Xie Shufang, Feng Li, and others marched up in force to Xuanwu Gate and killed the garrison commander.
proposals.after: The generals of Jiancheng's and Yuanji's palace establishments, Xue Wanche, Xie Shufang, Feng Li, and others, marched up in force to Xuanwu Gate and killed the garrison commander.
proposals.reason: 其宮府諸將 are the generals of both brothers' establishments, not Jiancheng's alone.

proposals.before: Jingde displayed the brothers' heads; the Eastern Palace troops scattered.
proposals.after: Jingde displayed Jiancheng's and Yuanji's heads; the palace-establishment troops thereupon scattered.
proposals.reason: 宮府兵 are the troops of both palace establishments, not the Eastern Palace only.

proposals.before: At a feast in Qingshan Palace he flew into a rage when a man of lower rank sat above him: "What have you done to rank above me?"
proposals.after: At a feast in Qingshan Palace he flew into a rage when someone whose place in the seating order was above him sat there: "What have you done that you should sit above me?"
proposals.reason: 班在其上者 means a person seated or ranked above him, not necessarily a man of lower official rank.

proposals.before: Once while attending a feast at Qingshan Palace, when someone of lower rank sat above him, Jingde angrily said: "What achievement have you, that you should sit above me?"
proposals.after: Once while attending a feast at Qingshan Palace, when there was someone whose place in the rank-order was above him, Jingde angrily said: "What achievement have you, that you should sit above me?"
proposals.reason: The Chinese does not say the other man was of lower rank; it says his ceremonial place was above Jingde.

proposals.before: In year 17 he petitioned to retire and was made grand master of the palace with gold seal, attending court on the first and fifteenth.
proposals.after: In year 17 he petitioned to retire and was made Grand Master Equal to the Three Palaces (kaifu yitong sansi), attending court on the first and fifteenth.
proposals.reason: 開府儀同三司 is not the gold-seal palace grand-master title; that rendering confuses it with 金紫光祿大夫.

proposals.before: The road to Liaodong is far; I fear there may be a change like Xuan Gan's.
proposals.after: The road to Liaodong is far; I fear there may be an uprising like Xuangan's.
proposals.reason: 玄感 is Yang Xuangan; splitting the name as Xuan Gan obscures the person.

proposals.before: The emperor refused and made him acting grand master of ceremonies and left first cavalry commander on the campaign that defeated Goryeo at Zhubeishan.
proposals.after: The emperor refused and made him acting grand master of ceremonies and left first cavalry commander on the campaign that defeated Goryeo at Mount Zhubi.
proposals.reason: 駐蹕山 is Zhubi (zhùbì), not Zhubei.

proposals.before: Gaozong mourned him, closed court three days, ordered officials of the fifth rank and above and tribute envoys to attend his funeral, and posthumously made him minister of works and military governor of Bingzhou with the posthumous name Loyal and Martial; he was buried at Zhaoling with imperial funeral honors.
proposals.after: Gaozong mourned him, closed court three days, ordered officials of the fifth rank and above and tribute envoys to attend his funeral, and posthumously made him Minister of Education (Situ) and military governor of Bingzhou with the posthumous name Loyal and Martial; he was buried at Zhaoling with imperial funeral honors.
proposals.reason: 司徒 is Situ, not Minister of Works (司空).

proposals.before: During the Sui he served in the guard of the general Lai Hu'er.
proposals.after: During the Daye reign he served in the guard of the Sui general Lai Hu'er.
proposals.reason: The Chinese dates the service to 大業中 (Daye), which the literal preserves but the idiomatic omits, collapsing it to a generic Sui setting.

proposals.before: Shubao despised Shichong's deceit; at Jiugqu, with Cheng Yaojin, Wu Heita, Niu Jinda, and dozens of riders, he rode west, dismounted, and said: "Though you have honored me, I cannot serve you—I take my leave."
proposals.after: Shubao despised Shichong's deceit; at Jiuqu, with Cheng Yaojin, Wu Heita, Niu Jinda, and dozens of riders, he rode west, dismounted, and said: "Though you have honored me, I cannot serve you—I take my leave."
proposals.reason: 九曲 is Jiuqu; Jiugqu is a corrupted romanization that obscures the place-name.

proposals.before: In the twelfth year he died; posthumously enfeoffed as Military Governor of Xuzhou and buried with honor at Zhaoling.
proposals.after: In the twelfth year he died; he was posthumously granted the office of Military Governor of Xuzhou and buried with honor at Zhaoling.
proposals.reason: 贈徐州都督 is a posthumous office grant, not an enfeoffment.

proposals.before: At Jiugqu, with Shubao and others, Zhijie bowed from horseback and said: "You have treated us well and we wished to repay you—
proposals.after: When Shichong resisted the imperial army at Jiuqu, Zhijie commanded troops in his formation; with Qin Shubao and others he bowed to Shichong from horseback and said: "You have treated us well and we wished to repay you—
proposals.reason: Idiomatic English misspells 九曲 as Jiugqu and omits Wang Shichong resisting the imperial army and Zhijie commanding in that formation.

proposals.before: He told the prince: "Your brothers have cut away your arms; you cannot last.
proposals.after: Zhijie told Taizong: "Your Highness's supporting arms have now all been cut away; you yourself cannot last long.
proposals.reason: 手臂 means supporting officers, not brothers; the speaker 知節白太宗 is also dropped.

proposals.before: Chuliang married Princess Changhe and became commandant of the horse and left guard middle general.
proposals.after: Chuliang, as the son of a meritorious minister, married Emperor Taizong's daughter the Grand Princess of Qinghe, and was appointed Commandant of the Horse and Left Guard Commandant of the Palace Gentlemen.
proposals.reason: 清河長公主 is Grand Princess of Qinghe, not Princess Changhe; 功臣子 and 太宗女 are omitted.

proposals.before: Chuliang, as son of a meritorious minister, married Emperor Taizong's daughter Princess Changhe of Qinghe, was appointed Commandant of the Horse and left guard middle general.
proposals.after: Chuliang, as son of a meritorious minister, married Emperor Taizong's daughter the Grand Princess of Qinghe, was appointed Commandant of the Horse and Left Guard Commandant of the Palace Gentlemen.
proposals.reason: 長公主 is Grand Princess; Changhe misreads 長, while 清河 is Qinghe.

proposals.before: He followed his father to Taiyuan and won the prince's favor.
proposals.after: Zhixuan followed his father at Taiyuan and was greatly received by Taizong.
proposals.reason: Chinese 太宗 is Taizong, not an unidentified prince.

proposals.before: He helped capture Qu Tuotong and was made flying-cavalry general of Leyou prefecture.
proposals.after: When Qu Tuotong fled, Zhixuan with the generals pursued and captured him; for merit he was appointed Flying Cavalry General of the Leyou garrison.
proposals.reason: 樂游府 is a garrison office (府), not a prefecture.

proposals.before: He won top credit in the defeats of Dou Jiande and Wang Shichong.
proposals.after: When Dou Jiande was defeated and the Eastern Capital pacified, his achievements again ranked among the greatest.
proposals.reason: Chinese 平東都 is the Eastern Capital, not Wang Shichong by name; the idiomatic invents Wang Shichong.

proposals.before: At the prince's accession he became left xiaoqi grand general, Duke of Fan, with nine hundred households.
proposals.after: When Taizong ascended the throne he was repeatedly promoted to Left Xiaoqi Grand General, enfeoffed as Duke of Fan, with a substantive fief of nine hundred households.
proposals.reason: 太宗即位 is Taizong's accession as emperor, not 'the prince's accession'.

proposals.before: He asked the rank go to his uncle Zhigan instead, and the emperor granted it.
proposals.after: Zhixuan kowtowed and firmly asked to transfer it to his mother's younger brother Zhigan; Taizong thereupon appointed Zhigan Left Guard Gentleman.
proposals.reason: 母弟 is specifically the mother's younger brother, not a generic uncle; the office grant is omitted.

proposals.before: Li Jiji and Yuchi Jingde recommended him and he entered the prince's staff.
proposals.after: At first he was not yet known by name; Li Ji and Yuchi Jingde also spoke of him, and he was then brought into the staff headquarters.
proposals.reason: 李勣 is Li Ji, not Li Jiji.

proposals.before: On the fourth day of the sixth month he waited at Xuanwu Gate with Zhangsun Wuji and eight others.
proposals.after: On the fourth day of the sixth month Gongjin with Zhangsun Wuji, among a party of nine, lay in ambush at Xuanwu Gate awaiting the change.
proposals.reason: 與長孫無忌等九人 is a group of nine including the named men; 'he ... and eight others' yields ten.

proposals.before: On the fourth day of the sixth month Gongjin with Zhangsun Wuji and nine others lay in ambush at Xuanwu Gate awaiting the change.
proposals.after: On the fourth day of the sixth month Gongjin with Zhangsun Wuji, among a party of nine, lay in ambush at Xuanwu Gate awaiting the change.
proposals.reason: 等九人 does not mean nine additional men besides Gongjin and Zhangsun.

proposals.before: The emperor mourned him; officials memorialized: "According to the Book of Yin and Yang, when the son is in chen one must not weep—it is also tabooed by common custom."
proposals.after: The emperor mourned him; officials memorialized: "According to the Book of Yin and Yang, when the day stands in chen one must not weep—it is also tabooed by common custom."
proposals.reason: 日子在辰 names a calendrical day in chen, not a son occupying chen.

proposals.before: Taizong heard and sighed in grief; he went out to halt and hold mourning; the relevant office memorialized: "According to the Book of Yin and Yang, on days when the son is in chen one cannot weep; it is also tabooed by floating custom."
proposals.after: Taizong heard and sighed in grief; he went out to halt and hold mourning; the relevant office memorialized: "According to the Book of Yin and Yang, on days when the date is in chen one cannot weep; it is also tabooed by floating custom."
proposals.reason: 日子在辰 is a hemerological day-branch, not a son.

proposals.before: Posthumously enfeoffed as Left Xiaoqi Grand General, posthumous name Xiang.
proposals.after: Posthumously granted Left Xiaoqi Grand General, posthumous name Xiang.
proposals.reason: 贈 of a guard generalship is a posthumous office grant, not an enfeoffment.

proposals.before: In the Yonghui reign he was again posthumously enfeoffed as Military Governor of Jingzhou.
proposals.after: In the Yonghui reign he was again posthumously granted Military Governor of Jingzhou.
proposals.reason: 贈荊州都督 is a posthumous office, not a fief.

proposals.before: Dasu served on the eastern terrace and edited the histories, compiling the Book of Later Wei in 100 juan and the Book of Sui in 30 scrolls.
proposals.after: Dasu in the Longshuo reign served as Eastern Terrace Attendant and concurrently compiled the national history; he died as Chief Administrator of Huaizhou, having written the Book of Later Wei in 100 juan and the Book of Sui in 30 juan.
proposals.reason: The idiomatic line omits Longshuo dating, concurrent national-history duty, and death in the Huaizhou post.

proposals.before: Da'an's son Shuang was chancellor of the directorate of education under Kaiyuan.
proposals.after: Da'an's son Shui was chancellor of the directorate of education under Kaiyuan.
proposals.reason: 涚 romanizes as Shui, not Shuang.

proposals.before: Da'an's son Shuang, in the Kaiyuan reign, was Chancellor of the Directorate of Education.
proposals.after: Da'an's son Shui, in the Kaiyuan reign, was Chancellor of the Directorate of Education.
proposals.reason: 涚 romanizes as Shui rather than Shuang.

decisions.reason: The Chinese names the captured prefectures as Jin and Hui (澮), not Fen (汾); the proposed Hui rendering is accurate.
晉、澮二州 is Jin and Hui; Fen is an unforced substitution for 澮.
柏壁 romanizes as Baibi; Baiyu does not match 壁.
The attack site is 柏壁 (Baibi), not Baiyu.
屈突通 is the compound-surname name Qutu Tong; Qu Tuotong splits 屈突 incorrectly.
李勣 is Li Ji; Li Jiji doubles the given name.

decisions.reason: 罪不容誅 means the crime exceeds what execution can atone for, not merely that death was deserved.
高祖 jailed him for interrogation and was going to kill him; 太宗固諫得釋 is firm remonstrance securing release, not an unnamed desperate plea.

其宮府諸將 follows both Jiancheng and Yuanji; the generals belong to both palace establishments, not Jiancheng alone.

decisions.reason: 班在其上者 is a person whose place in the seating or rank-order was above Jingde, not a man of lower rank.
The Chinese states that someone’s 班 was above Jingde; it does not call that person lower-ranking.
開府儀同三司 is Grand Master Equal to the Three Palaces, not the gold-seal palace grand-master title 金紫光祿大夫.

decisions.reason: 玄感 is the personal name Xuangan (Yang Xuangan); splitting it as Xuan Gan and rendering 變 as a vague 'change' obscures the rebellion.
駐蹕山 is Mount Zhubi (zhùbì); Zhubei misreads 蹕.
冊贈司徒 is Situ (Minister of Education), not Minister of Works (司空).

The line has Shichong resisting the imperial army at 九曲 and Zhijie commanding in that formation; Jiugqu and the omitted military setting are errors.

decisions.reason: 清河長公主 is the Grand Princess of Qinghe, daughter of Taizong; Princess Changhe misreads 長, and 功臣子 is omitted in the original.

decisions.reason: 樂游府 is a garrison office, not a prefecture, but the proposal still splits 屈突通 as Qu Tuotong; Qutu Tong is required.

decisions.reason: 平東都 is pacifying the Eastern Capital; naming Wang Shichong here is not in this sentence.

decisions.reason: 贈荊州都督 is a posthumous office, not a fief.

claimRevisions.reason: The extracted English personal name Qu Tuotong was produced by splitting the compound surname 屈突; the source names Qutu Tong.
